statement: Three cubes weigh the same as two balls. One ball and one cube together weigh 50 grams. How many grams does one cube weigh?

choices.misconception: I divided 50 by 5 because the first fact has 3 cubes and 2 balls.
I split the 50 grams equally, as if a ball and a cube weighed the same.
I found the weight of a ball instead of a cube.
I worked out what three cubes weigh, which is one side of the balance, not one cube.

hints: Try doubling the second fact: what do two balls and two cubes weigh?
Two balls and two cubes weigh 100 grams. Swap the two balls for something the first fact says weighs the same, so only cubes are left. Then share the weight among the cubes.
Two balls weigh the same as three cubes, so two balls and two cubes weigh the same as five cubes, which is 100 grams.

solutions.reliable: One ball and one cube weigh 50 g, so two balls and two cubes weigh 100 g. Two balls weigh the same as three cubes, so this is the same as five cubes. Five cubes weigh 100 g, so one cube weighs 20 g. Check: a ball is 50 - 20 = 30 g, and three cubes (60 g) balance two balls (60 g). The transferable idea: on a balance, swap things of equal weight until only one kind is left.
solutions.elegant: Back-solve: if a cube is 20 g then a ball is 30 g, and 3 x 20 = 2 x 30. No other choice balances.

whyOnTest: Balance puzzles reward swapping equal weights until one kind of object remains, and the distractors stop or split too soon.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
